retier_note: The planning documents refer to this beat as the Q23 answer. DP03 is the bank id that carries it: the question asks which regions customer data is stored or processed in, and the answer names customer records in an EU environment, contradicting the declared scope of internal analytics only.

AC01.text: Multi-factor authentication is enforced organisation-wide. Every user account across every environment requires MFA, including administrative access.
AC01.note: The hero contradiction. The vendor's own audit report records an unremediated exception for administrative access.

IR01.text: Our contractual breach notification window is 24 hours from detection, which we consider best in class for our sector.
IR01.note: Contradicted by the incident sheet, which records a 9-day disclosure.

CP01.text: Our most recent SOC 2 Type II report is attached, covering 1 July 2024 to 30 June 2025. The auditor is Kestrel Assurance Partners and the opinion is qualified.

DP01.text: We follow industry best practice for encryption both at rest and in transit.
DP01.note: The deliberately vague answer. Below the confidence threshold, so it triggers one targeted follow-up quoting the answer back and naming the evidence required.

DP03.text: Shipment data is processed in our primary region. Customer records are processed in our EU environment for route optimisation and are retained there for 18 months.
DP03.note: Re-tier trigger. Intake declared internal operational data with no customer data; this answer names customer records, so the tier moves from 2 to 1 and the additional domain's questions go out mid-flight.

CP03.text: The report records one exception relating to access review timing, which has been addressed.
CP03.note: The report actually records two exceptions, one of which is unremediated.

AC02.text: Privileged access is granted by the platform team and reviewed periodically.

IR02.text: We had one security incident in the last 24 months, in March 2025, affecting a shipment metadata store. It was contained and disclosed to affected customers.

CP04.text: ISO/IEC 27001 certificate number ISO-27001-DD-2298, issued by Ravenscroft Certification Ltd. The certificate is attached.
CP04.note: The attached certificate expired on 14 March 2025. The vendor does not mention this. The deterministic expiry check catches it without a model call.

SP01.text: Our subprocessor list is attached. Four subprocessors, all within the EU.

DP02.text: Shipment records are retained for 36 months. Customer records in the EU environment are retained for 18 months.

AC03.text: Access is revoked promptly on departure, usually within a day or two.

BC01.text: RTO is 8 hours and RPO is 1 hour. Our last recovery test was in 2024.
